original_topic: empirical reply-to-proposition alignment in email and dialogue, focusing on partial replies, multiple questions, unanswered questions, and multi-proposition antecedents
topic: empirical reply-scope and question-answer alignment in real email or multi-party dialogue, emphasizing partial replies to individual propositions or questions, unanswered-question detection, and responses with multiple proposition antecedents
focus: academic gaps of the previous round

prior_gaps.description: Direct empirical evidence is still missing for proposition-level agreement, rejection, approval, clarification, and answer scope in authentic workplace email or enterprise chat, especially cases where one short response applies to only part of a preceding message.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "reply scope" workplace email dialogue proposition agreement approval rejection clarification partial reply

prior_gaps.description: The corpus still does not establish a validated annotation and evaluation scheme for mapping workplace responses to exact proposition or span targets while representing exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, and potentially multiple antecedents.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve through annotation-guideline and benchmark design rather than additional literature search: define the target unit and admissible antecedent structures; specify labels for exact, partial, ambiguous, unsupported, discontinuous, and multiple antecedents; create adjudication rules and difficult-case examples; annotate a representative workplace dataset with multiple annotators; measure inter-annotator agreement separately for target-span selection and relation labels; and validate evaluation metrics on gold and predicted candidate sets, including exact match, overlap or span-level measures, multi-antecedent scoring, and abstention handling.

prior_gaps.description: Direct evidence remains insufficient for aligning replies to one or more questions when a preceding workplace message contains multiple questions, requests, or alternatives, including detection of questions that remain unanswered.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "multiple questions" dialogue reply alignment partial answer unanswered question email conversation

prior_gaps.description: It remains open whether and how a workplace response should be modeled as targeting a composite or multi-proposition antecedent. The corpus supports composite abstract discourse referents theoretically and multi-antecedent entity reference analogically, but provides no direct evaluation of multi-proposition reply scope in work communication.
prior_gaps.suggested_search_query: "multi-proposition antecedent" dialogue response composite discourse referent split antecedent reply

prior_gaps.description: The appropriate abstention, ambiguity, and missing-antecedent policy for msgloom remains unvalidated. The relative cost of an over-broad approval or commitment link versus leaving a link unresolved requires an explicit product-risk cost model and dedicated benchmark.
prior_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve with a product-specific risk model and benchmark. Define error categories such as over-broad commitment or approval links, wrong antecedent, unresolved but recoverable links, ambiguity, and missing context; assign operational costs with stakeholder input; construct a benchmark containing high-risk approval, commitment, partial-reply, ambiguous, and missing-antecedent cases; evaluate confidence thresholds, abstention policies, and ambiguity states under the chosen cost function; and select policy thresholds based on expected product risk rather than literature-derived defaults.
